title: RAW UNREVIEWED: f77r P2 reintroduces an upstream port or starts a new subject
summary: GDT790 records exact otedy at an upper-arch port and at the start of the separate f77r P2 record; GDT791 quarantines older automatic participant inheritance across that visible panel boundary. Freeze the complete upper and middle panels and P1/P2 prose. One reading would explicitly reintroduce the arch port as the input or cause of a downstream operation; a rival treats the P2 opener as a new record head with no transported participant. Require an independently traceable physical connection and an overt text bridge beyond the repeated head, preserving GDT118's missing-data objection. This is a fresh whole-discourse question, not a rescue of GDT180's post hoc quality sequence or of the quarantined alias.

design.mechanism: a cross-panel record may refer overtly to a specific earlier labeled port and its downstream consequence
design.unit: complete f77r upper and middle admitted panels with full P1 and P2 records
design.contrast: explicit cross-panel port-to-operation relation versus independent new-record heading
design.prediction: a fixed whole reading must bind the visible port, an independently traced connection and a non-head overt participant in P2; absent any of these means no semantic test
